page: Amazon Web Services m4.large is a general-purpose fourth-generation instance type. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.4 GHz, configured with 2 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the m4.large sits in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1260.98 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 1666.09 (bottom 10%). Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached read and write bandwidths of 12.28 GB/sec and 10.68 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 948.0 and a multi-core score of 1148.0.

Given the baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps and the absence of local storage, the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage. Database operations under Passmark scored 618.18, and Redis SET operations reached 0.75 million operations per second. These metrics, combined with a static web serving throughput of 1.85 GB/sec, suggest the instance is suited for lightweight, non-critical general-purpose workloads, basic development environments, or legacy applications that do not require high computational density or modern instruction sets like AVX-512.
